summary: TERRA TWIN X is a web app that finds and characterizes places on Earth that best match future Moon and Mars landing and base sites. A user picks a target (such as Jezero Crater on Mars or Shackleton Crater Rim on the Moon) and an experiment type (rover mobility, ISRU, EVA and habitats, astrobiology or drilling). The app scores 26 Earth sites — and any spot the user clicks — from 0 to 100% on six factors (geology, topography, thermal regime, aridity, radiation exposure and regolith), using live NASA POWER climate data. For every site it shows NASA satellite imagery, real ground photos, a narrated “Why this score?” video, and an Environmental Delta Matrix that says exactly where Earth differs from the target and how to compensate in field tests. This helps mission teams choose better analog sites, test hardware more realistically, and lower mission risk before flying to the Moon or Mars.
details:
What it does. TERRA TWIN X answers one question: which place on Earth best matches a given Moon or Mars site for a given experiment — and where does it fall short?

How it works.

  1. Mission setup: choose Mars or the Moon, one of six targets (Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Arcadia Planitia, Shackleton Crater Rim, Mare Tranquillitatis Skylight, Aristarchus Plateau) and an experiment type.
  2. Planetary Analog Matching (PAM): each Earth site gets a 0–1 score on six vectors. Geology, topography and regolith compare rock, landform and surface classes. Thermal, aridity and radiation use NASA POWER climatology (mean temperature, day–night range, precipitation, humidity, surface sunlight, elevation), scored by how far each value sits toward the planetary extreme of Earth’s range. Experiment-specific weights combine them into a 0–100% match. A data-coverage score shows how many of the six vectors have data, flagging sites that need field characterization.
  3. Discovery mode: click anywhere on Earth to fetch that point’s NASA climate data and score it, or scan a 5×5 grid around it for new candidates.
  4. For each site: NASA GIBS satellite views, geotagged photos from Wikimedia Commons, an Environmental Delta Matrix (gravity, pressure, temperature, water, radiation, regolith), a compensated field-test plan, and a narrated “Why this score?” explainer video.
  5. Validation mode: checks that established analog sites outscore obvious non-analogs (e.g. London, Manaus) for every target and experiment.

Benefits. It turns analog-site choice into a data-driven decision, says honestly where Earth tests can’t represent the Moon or Mars, and points to sites (including under-studied ones like Lonar Crater, the Rann of Kutch and Spiti Valley in India) that deserve field study.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks; canvas-rendered globes; NASA POWER and NASA GIBS APIs; Wikimedia Commons API; ElevenLabs text-to-speech (optional narration); hosted on GitHub Pages. Code: https://github.com/Hridhaan27/terra-twin-x

Limitations and next steps. NASA POWER data is on a ~0.5° grid, so mountains and small craters are smoothed. Next: per-pixel terrain (SRTM / Copernicus DEM), mineralogy (EMIT), thermal inertia (ECOSTRESS vs THEMIS/Diviner), and target climate from the Mars Climate Database.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) climatology API, 2001–2020 means: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2M_RANGE, PRECTOTCORR, RH2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, PS and grid elevation. Fetched live for every site and any clicked point.
